description: The Earth Dragon in Chinese astrology: personality, Earth element traits, 1928 and 1988 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Earth Dragon is the Dragon born in a Earth year, one of five versions of the fifth animal. It combines the Dragon's vitality with Earth's qualities. Earth Dragon years between 1924 and 2044 are 1928 and 1988. The Dragon's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Earth Dragon personality
paragraphs: When the stem matches the sign's own element, as it does for the Earth Dragon, readings describe a particularly grounded, steady version of a famously flamboyant animal. The Dragon always carries Earth, so a second layer of Earth adds patience, practicality and a sense of responsibility to its natural ambition. Earth Dragons are often pictured as fair, reliable and sensible, preferring well-planned achievement to dramatic gestures. They tend to be loyal friends and dependable leaders who build institutions rather than chase applause. Doubled Earth can also bring stubbornness and a fondness for control. Once an Earth Dragon has settled on a view, readings suggest, shifting it may require considerable evidence and time.

Earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind. Descriptions associate it with reliability, honesty and a talent for holding things together, whether that means a family, a budget or a team in a difficult season. Earth-year people are often portrayed as grounded, fair and good at turning ideas into workable plans. The element is linked with nourishment and care, so it carries a quiet generosity. Its shadow, in most readings, is heaviness: worry, stubbornness and a reluctance to move until every risk has been weighed twice.

sections.heading: Earth Dragon at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Earth is usually associated with management, organisation and long-term stewardship. Earth-year people are often described as the steady hands who keep systems running, look after budgets and notice when colleagues are struggling, which suits administration, property, finance, agriculture, healthcare and operations. They tend to earn trust slowly and keep it. The traditional caution is resistance to change: an Earth stem may hold on to a process after it has stopped working, so regular reviews and a willingness to experiment help.

The Earth Dragon is often pictured as a builder-king, ambitious yet patient enough to pour solid foundations. Corporate strategy, real estate, government, large-scale engineering and institution-building suit it, since vision there has to survive committees and spreadsheets. It respects competence, prefers fair procedures and earns trust by delivering exactly what it promised. In close relationships this Dragon is protective, generous and dependable, eager to provide comfort and standing for the family. It needs appreciation for the responsibility it carries, voiced rather than assumed. Friction shows up around authority: because it shoulders so much, an Earth Dragon may assume its plan for holidays, budgets or schooling should simply prevail.

sections.heading: Earth Dragon years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Earth Dragon years are 1928 (January 23, 1928 to February 9, 1929) and 1988 (February 17, 1988 to February 5, 1989). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1988 anyone born before Feb 17 is a Fire Rabbit, not a Earth Dragon. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Earth Dragon year is Yang, matching the Dragon's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Wu-Chen, joining the heavenly stem Wu to the earthly branch Chen. Births just before each new year fall in the Fire Rabbit year (before January 23, 1928) and the Fire Rabbit year (before February 17, 1988), and births in the weeks after each Earth Dragon year ends belong to the Earth Snake. The new year itself fell on a Monday in 1928 and Wednesday in 1988.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Earth Dragon
paragraphs: The useful challenge for an Earth Dragon is flexibility. Inviting dissent on purpose, perhaps by asking colleagues to argue the opposite case, helps balance its natural certainty. Because the combination carries responsibility easily, it may also take too much on itself and resent others for not helping; asking directly works better. Earth Dragons often benefit from creative or playful pursuits that have no practical purpose, which lighten doubled Earth's seriousness. Travelling and meeting people from very different backgrounds widens their perspective. When their steadiness stays open to new information, Earth Dragons become wise and trusted pillars of their communities.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Earth Dragon shares the Dragon's San He trine with the Rat and Monkey (the Water trine), its Liu He bond with the Rooster, and its Liu Chong clash with the Dog. The element adds a second layer: another Earth sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Earth in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Earth Dragon years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1928 (from January 23, 1928) and 1988 (from February 17, 1988). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Earth Dragon's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Earth and the Dragon's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles earth year element matches the fixed element. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Earth Dragon?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rat and Monkey (San He) and the Rooster (Liu He). The Dog is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Earth Dragon called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Wu-Chen. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Earth stem Wu, followed by its earthly branch, here Chen for the Dragon, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Earth Dragon different from other Dragons?
faq.answer: All Dragons share vitality, ambition and confidence. The Earth year element changes the tone: earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind.
